entries.title: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure and charters out tankers into October, sources say
entries.claimSummary: QatarEnergy extended force majeure for LNG supplies to several Asian buyers into mid-September.
extractedFacts: Force-majeure notices due to expire in August and early September were extended until mid-September.
Affected buyers include customers in South Korea, India and Bangladesh.
QatarEnergy continued leasing some LNG tankers through mid-October.
At least nine QELM/QET-controlled LNG carriers were sub-chartered to named third parties.
entries.carryReason: No newer source-verified QatarEnergy force-majeure notice was approved in the Aug 11 review; the Reuters July 23 notice extending force majeure through mid-September remains the latest approved disclosure, with the mid-October extension still unconfirmed preparation.

entries.title: Strait of Hormuz Crossings Rise 8% Week-on-Week, But Dark AIS Activity Remains Elevated
entries.claimSummary: Kpler vessel-type data reported via Foreign Policy Journal shows 3 LNG tanker transits among 106 total Hormuz crossings during Jul 27-Aug 2, the first LNG-specific movement since the carried July 18 zero-transit observation.
extractedFacts: The week of Jul 27-Aug 2 recorded 106 total crossings by 96 distinct vessels, up 8% from 98 crossings the prior week.
Vessel-type breakdown of the 106 crossings included 3 LNG tankers, 40 liquid tankers, 24 bulk carriers, and smaller counts of other vessel types.
Dark AIS activity (undetermined routes) covered 41% of crossings, down from 49% the prior week.
entries.carryReason: No newer source-verified weekly Kpler LNG-transit breakdown was approved in the Aug 11 review; the Aug 3 Foreign Policy Journal count of 3 LNG transits for the week of Jul 27-Aug 2 remains the latest approved figure.

entries.title: Trump demands compensation from Iran as talks on Strait of Hormuz continue
entries.claimSummary: Al Jazeera's Aug 11 report, citing MarineTraffic data, said Hormuz crossings fell from 15 on Friday to 11 on Saturday to 6 on Sunday, with 17 vessels routed via the Iran-designated lane and 10 classified as undetermined.
extractedFacts: MarineTraffic data showed Hormuz crossings went from 15 on Friday to 11 on Saturday, and six on Sunday.
Of Sunday's crossings, 17 vessels passed through the Iran-designated route, while 10 others took a route classified as undetermined.
President Trump said the US will seek compensation from Iran for '50 years' of alleged damages.
Trump said the US Navy has swept the Strait of Hormuz of mines and now holds '100%' control of the waterway.
